interesting_facts: The 1988 EP title 'Abbiamo Pazientato 40 Anni: Ora Basta!' quotes a Mussolini speech, and the cover depicts Balilla (fascist youth). Yet it was released by the most radically anarchist hardcore label in Italy — a deliberate, intelligent political provocation.
The 1991 EP 'Crisi di Valori' sampled the voice of Pope John Paul II in its title track — a bold act of cultural subversion in a predominantly Catholic country.
Rolling Stone Italia described them as 'l'argine rock all'Emilia rossa' — the rock dam holding back the dominance of left-wing cultural hegemony in Emilia-Romagna.
Their live shows featured extraordinary guest performers: the Alpine Choir of Monte Calisio, Mondine (female rice paddy workers from Bentivoglio), and a choir of Alpini (Italian Alpine troops).
Founding guitarist Dario Parisini died June 9, 2022, aged 56, after a long illness. The Dish-Is-Nein 12" single 'The Metal Machine' was dedicated to him.
The successor band name 'Dish-Is-Nein' is a triple pun: German-sounding 'This is no,' English 'This is none,' and phonetically evokes 'Disciplinatha' in Italian.
While their debut EP was raw and technically unrefined, Parisini himself noted it 'has aged much better than Primigenia' (their final, more polished album).

Dish-Is-Nein's 2025 album 'Occidente (A Funeral Party)' was hailed by critics as one of the best albums of that year, proving the project's enduring creative vitality 38+ years after Disciplinatha's formation.

demotape_archive_notes.assessment: Disciplinatha is a crucial band for understanding the Italian underground punk/industrial scene of the late 1980s and 1990s. Their deliberate provocations, fusion of genres, and connection to the Emilian punk lineage make them highly relevant to the Demotape archive.
